title: Consumers Can Handle a Stock Crash
gist: Jason Furman estimates that an AI-bubble stock crash of 25% would cut consumption ~0.8% and GDP growth only ~0.6pp via the wealth effect, because households have spent only ~1 cent per dollar of recent stock gains (vs ~3 cents historically). He finds the 2001 recession was the least consumer-driven postwar recession, though stocks are now a record 286% of GDP so a 25% fall wipes out wealth comparable to the 2000–02 halving.
